newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FOCUS-Retailing Portuguese banks go head to head.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Retailing Portuguese banks go head to head.

text.p: A new bank owned jointly by Banco Comercial Portugues SA (BCP) and retail chain Jeronimo Martins will compete head on with Portugal's biggest retailer Sonae, which has said it will open its own bank, analysts said on Thursday.
"Jeronimo Martins (JM) could not lag behind Sonae," said Jose Freire, analyst with Lisbon research house Gesfinc.

Estabelecimentos Jeronimo Martins e Filhos and BCP said on Wednesday they had signed an agreement to launch a bank owned equally by both groups that would offer in-store financial services to customers in JM hypermarkets and supermarkets.
The deal, subject to the approval of Portuguese regulatory authorities, follows an announcement by Sonae that it will open its own retail bank, Universo Banco Directo.
Analysts said Sonae's bank, financed wholly by the retailer and expected to open early next year, would probably operate branches in Sonae's shopping centres.
Both retail banks should offer consumer credit facilities such as mortgages, car loans and insurance products, they said.
"These retailers have seen a clear market," said Anusha Govindjee, equities analyst with Lisbon bank Banco Efisa.

The two big Portuguese retailers were following in the footsteps of big foreign retail chains such as Britain's Marks & Spencer Plc and Selfridges and the United States' Bloomingdales which already offer financial services.

Analysts said they did not expect Portugal's third biggest retailer Pao de Acucar, bought recently by private French group Auchan, to follow suit and open a retail bank as its customer base was probably too small to justify such a move.
All Portugal's big three retailers already offer credit cards to customers.
Gesfinc's Freire said he expected JM's retail bank to open by the end of this year, a few months ahead of Sonae's bank.
"JM had a different strategy to Sonae. They have formed an alliance with a bank, while Sonae for now are going alone," he said.
Govindjee said: "BCP will provide the financial know-how to JM."
Freire said it was hard to predict the impact of the new banks on the turnover of JM and Sonae, but he expected JM's bank to turn a profit by 1998.
Analysts said the big retailers should compete strongly with banks in providing credit facilities as they already benefited from strong cash flows in their supermarkets and hypermarkets.
Govindjee said the retailers would have to market their financial services aggressively in order to compete, by offering incentives based on retail purchases.

Shares in both JM and BCP rose in morning trade on Lisbon bourse as the market welcomed the news of the proposed bank and a statement by JM Finance Director Jorge Ponce de Leao that JM would like to buy gradually up to 1.5 percent of BCP's capital.

JM stood at 14,600 escudos, up 400, in light volume of 912 shares and BCP traded at 1,860 escudos, up 30, in volume of 14,740 shares in the late morning. Sonae was steady, trading at 4,400 escudos, up one, in low volume of 1,024 shares.
One dealer said: "It is very positive for JM that it will offer a range of financial services to its customers, increasing its client base and customer loyalty."
